identity_marker: green Raspberry Pi 4 Model B circuit board with silver ports
continuity_anchors: on a clean wooden desk under bright, even studio lighting
video_goal: Visually guide the user through flashing an SD card and physically connecting the components to boot up a Raspberry Pi 4.
single_prompt: From an overhead view, hands place a green Raspberry Pi 4 Model B circuit board with silver ports, a MicroSD card, and a black USB-C power supply side-by-side on a clean wooden desk under bright, even studio lighting. The camera moves to a close-up as fingers slide the MicroSD card into a USB SD card reader, then push the reader into the USB port of a laptop. Transitioning to a screen capture, the mouse cursor clicks the white 'CHOOSE OS' button within the pink and white Raspberry Pi Imager UI, scrolls down the pop-up list, and clicks on the 'Raspberry Pi OS (32-bit)' option. The cursor then clicks 'CHOOSE STORAGE', selects the mounted SD card drive, and clicks the 'WRITE' button, showing a progress bar filling up. Back to a close-up, fingers pull the USB SD card reader out of the laptop and extract the MicroSD card. Hands flip the green Raspberry Pi 4 Model B circuit board with silver ports upside down and slide the MicroSD card into the metal slot on the bottom edge until it is flush. From an over-the-shoulder view, hands plug a micro-HDMI cable into the first small port labeled 'HDMI0'. In a close-up, hands plug a USB mouse cable and a USB keyboard cable into the two silver USB 2.0 ports, then fingers push the USB-C power cable firmly into the USB-C port. A macro shot reveals a solid red LED and a rapidly blinking green LED illuminating on the corner of the board. Finally, the camera shows a monitor view as the connected screen transitions from black to the Raspberry Pi OS desktop, displaying a sunset wallpaper and a 'Welcome to Raspberry Pi' dialog box.
